questions.question: What is a token in the context of LLMs?
options: A sub-word chunk of text, the basic unit LLMs process, bill on, and rate-limit against
A security credential for API access
questions.explanation: Tokens are typically sub-word pieces of text produced by a tokenizer, and they are the actual unit of measurement for cost, rate limits, and context window size.

questions.question: Why do embedding-based semantic search systems return documents that don't share exact keywords with a query?
options: This is always a bug in the retrieval system
Embeddings represent meaning as vectors, and texts with similar meaning end up with similar vectors even without shared exact words
Semantic search ignores the query entirely
Embeddings only work for numeric data
questions.explanation: Embeddings capture meaning rather than exact wording, so a query like 'cheap flights' can match a document saying 'affordable airfare' because their vectors are close, even with no overlapping keywords.

questions.question: A product team is surprised that non-English queries cost more per request than similar-length English queries. Which question best explains this?
options: Is this a billing error that needs to be reported immediately?
Have we measured actual token counts (not word or character counts) for our supported languages, since tokenization efficiency varies by language?
Should we just stop supporting non-English languages?
Is the API provider overcharging us on purpose?
questions.explanation: Different languages and scripts often tokenize less efficiently than English, producing more tokens for a similar amount of content — a predictable, well-understood effect rather than a billing error.
